en: The Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti Mānasika-pūjā-stotra (The Mental Worship Hymn to the Auspicious Dakṣiṇāmūrti)
I worship Him who holds a mudrā, a rosary, a skull-bowl, and the sciences; who is joined with a tiger skin, a crescent moon, and the lord of serpents;
who is the rain-cloud for the minds of the lords of yogis; who is the bee at the lotus of the heart; and whose southern face is radiant.
He stands clearly near the banyan tree, shining while being praised, with a tiger skin bound as an upper garment upon his powerful arms.
I meditate upon the Lord of Sages, the moon-crested one, whose face is turned to the south, whose eyes are flickering, and whose body is like a mass of crystal.
(2) I invoke the Great Soul Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, adorned with beautiful serpents, his five-fingered hand marked by the *vijñānamudrā*, and shining with the application of sacred ash as unguent. (3)
O Lord, remain firm upon this pedestal joined with gold, jewels, pure vajras, sapphires, rubies, pearls, and gems; be the bestower of boons, for I shall install you, the southern face.
O Lord, having brought the pure water of the glorious Gaṅgā, I shall offer it for the sake of your beautiful form.
O Lord whose lotus-face is serene, who are worshipped by the world, I offer this southern face of yours for the three periods of time.
O you whose limbs are marked by ornaments of rudrākṣa beads, accept this [offering] mixed with musk.
O abode of the universe, which is unassailable throughout the three periods of time, I shall present the water for the feet (pādya) within my heart to your southern face.
O Ānanda, worshipped by the lords of the gods, I shall joyfully offer you this water from the river Gaṅgā;
O Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, whose very nature is that of the Guru, perform your ritual rinsing of the mouth now.
Sprinkle [the deity] with ghee, milk, curd, honey, and sugar;
O Lord, perform this bath of the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) while facing south.
O Śūlapāṇi, who is to be known through the Vedāntas and who is worshipped by Brahmā, Indra, and the lords of the gods!
Perform your bath in these pure waters of the Gaṅgā, well-scented; O you who face the south, perform it here.
I wipe your stainless limbs, O Lord of Gods, with a silken cloth.
O you who are gracious to the three worlds known as Prajñā, O Śrī Dakṣiṇāmukha, protector of all the worlds!
O Lord, put on this excellent sacred thread made of golden threads, O God.
O Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, whose arms, belly, and five faces are vast, O you whose very nature is bliss!

11 O Great-Souled One, whose southern face dwells in the heart of Gaurī, I shall joyfully offer this fragrant scent, mixed with musk, sandalwood, saffron, and other ingredients, contained within a jeweled vessel. 12
O Supreme Self, I shall worship you with pure unbroken rice grains well-mixed with white sesame seeds; O blissful one, I shall always do so with a concentration solely fixed upon you, O Dakṣiṇāmūrti,
who are adorned with excellent jewels, a crown, earrings, necklaces, rings, bracelets, and a girdle.
I worship Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, who holds a crescent moon and a vessel of nectar upon his crest.
(14) I shall forever worship the great form of Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, who nourishes the entire multitude of worlds within his belly, with variegated flowers placed upon pearls and gems. (15)
I offer this ten-ingredient incense, blended with various fragrances and clarified butter.
O Omniscient One named Medha, honored by the lords of sages, Digambara, facing south, please accept it.
(16) This lamp, mixed with clarified butter, provided with three wicks, and joined with fire—
Accept what is offered by me, O Lord of Yogins; be gracious, O venerable Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti!

(17) O South-facing One, partake of this rice with pure soup, vegetables, and various foods mixed with clarified butter and sprinkled with curd, along with wood-apples, excellent grapes, and mangoes, accompanied by the ritual sipping of water (āpośana). (18)
O Lord of Sacrifice, O Destroyer of Desire, O Embodiment of Merit, O You whose southern face is pure, drink this water mixed with molasses, rock salt, buttermilk, camphor, sandalwood,
and cloves. O God, Lord of the Clouds, quickly perform the *uttarāpośana* rite with the water falling from the path of the sky.
O Śarva, perform the washing of your pair of hands; O south-facing one, take a mouthful of water.

Perform the ritual sipping (*ācamana*) properly with water; may you be at ease in the region to my left. O pure form of consciousness, whose every desire is fulfilled, this purifying [water] has been prepared for you, O south-facing one. (20–21)
O south-facing one, today accept this betel-roll, prepared with camphor, pearl powder, and manikya gems,
along with pieces of areca nut and betel leaves of many forms and colors;
and accept this lustration rite (*nīrājana*), placed in a stainless vessel, illuminated by camphor, and manifesting my own form.
O Lord, O Śaṅkara, whose form is the sky and whose face is turned to the south, I offer this to you. 23.
Thereafter, O Lord, whose southern face is purifying, behold this mirror, bright as the sun that illuminates the world, fashioned from rubies, pearls, gems, gold, and sapphires. 24.
I offer this handful of fragrant flowers— mandāra, lotus, kunda, and jājī— to you,
O Dakṣiṇāmūrti who assumes diverse forms, whose pair of hands are adorned with the trident and the ḍhakka drum.
I shall perform a perfect circumambulation of you, who are delightful in your compassion, throughout the three periods of time.
O Lord of the auspicious mind, forgive my transgression, O Lord of Sacrifice, whose face is the sacrificial fee!
26 Salutations again and again to the destroyer of sins; salutations again and again to the one worshipped by the lotus-born Brahmā;
salutations again and again to the Great Lord Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, who resides in the heart of Kṛṣṇa! 27
Thus ends the Śrī-Dakṣiṇāmūrti-Mānasika-pūjā-stotra composed by Vijñānendra.
